queue_items.grounds: This row's own device_notes reasons from the subordination -- the frame כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier) is preceded by כִּי (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier), so the formula is not verse-initial. That is byte-true, and it is equally byte-true of כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ (oshb:Isa.52.4, byte tier) against כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte tier), where the same construction is treated as a fresh frame onset opening a new unit. The construction is one object book-wide: it stands at 14 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier (sweep: 14 verses, word-bound and substring counts agreeing), oshb:Isa.52.3, oshb:Isa.52.4 and oshb:Isa.56.4 among them, and all three sit on the divine side of the koh-amar census. No field in either row names a discriminator, so the warrant column is incoherent across the batch. Recorded, not adjudicated: both seams rest on a ruled tier-1 frame onset standing in their own bytes, so no respan is proposed here.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: state the discriminating principle that lets a verse-initial conjunction plus messenger formula reinforce an ongoing frame here while opening a fresh one at web:Isa.52.4 -- or route the pair for a single adjudicated ruling.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: This row opens on the messenger frame כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.56.1), which launches the divine command “Maintain justice and do what is right, for my salvation is near and my righteousness will soon be revealed.” (web:Isa.56.1). The command sets the terms for the admission promise that follows: the foreigner who fears being excluded and the eunuch who calls himself “a dry tree” (web:Isa.56.3) are answered by a second, reinforcing instance of the same messenger formula at web:Isa.56.4 (oshb:Isa.56.4), promising those eunuchs “a memorial and a name better than of sons and of daughters” (web:Isa.56.5) and the foreigners a standing “for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.” (web:Isa.56.7). The row holds the general sabbath-and-justice exhortation of web:Isa.56.1-Isa.56.2 together with the foreigner/eunuch oracle of web:Isa.56.3-Isa.56.7 as one admission unit rather than opening a fresh row at the third-person turn of web:Isa.56.3, since no new addressee or frame marker intervenes there and the same messenger frame governs both. The row closes with Isa.56.8, whose divine signature נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.56.8, the adonai-YHWH form) stands verse-initial and heads the gathering clause it introduces -- “I will yet gather others to him, in addition to his own who are gathered.” (web:Isa.56.8) -- rather than closing or sealing it; the formula class is postpositive elsewhere across the book's koh-amar/neum census, but this instance opens its own clause. The row ends the verse just before the addressee shift to the summoned field animals at web:Isa.56.9.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading opens a fresh row at the third-person turn of web:Isa.56.3, treating the sabbath-and-justice exhortation of web:Isa.56.1-Isa.56.2 as a separate short unit from the foreigner/eunuch admission oracle.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: salvation oracle admitting foreigners and eunuchs to Yahweh's house and covenant

shipped_row.device_notes: This row's own front seam Isa.55.13 and its interior verses Isa.56.2, Isa.56.3, and Isa.56.5 each carry setumah breaks (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only, never a driver here). Separately, oshb:Isa.56.4 carries a single paseq seg (count-only, no intra-verse position claimed), an unrelated disclosure class. The messenger frame opening Isa.56.1, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.56.1), and the frame at Isa.56.4, כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.56.4), collate against each other at consonantal-skeleton tier only: the opening letter of the first carries a dagesh that the second lacks, so the two fail even accent-stripped tier, and the Isa.56.4 instance is not itself verse-initial, standing after the subordinating כִּי that opens that verse. Both sit on the divine side of the book-wide koh-amar census (44 of 48 verses per the current inventory classification), not the royal-messenger side confined to 4 sites in the chs 36-37 narrative zone. The unit's real internal cohesion is a byte-identical refrain pair bracketing the third-person turn: שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ (byte tier) recurs between Isa.56.2 and Isa.56.6 (oshb:Isa.56.2, oshb:Isa.56.6), and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי (byte tier) recurs between Isa.56.4 and Isa.56.6 (oshb:Isa.56.4, oshb:Isa.56.6). Separately, this row's own front seam carries a cross-seam echo: the closing run לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת (byte tier) is shared by the verse just before this row's span, Isa.55.13 (that verse's own ketiv/qere note sits earlier in it, outside the quoted words), and this row's own Isa.56.5 (oshb:Isa.55.13, oshb:Isa.56.5), a byte-identical pair straddling the front boundary, standing at byte tier in exactly two verses book-wide; its consonantal skeleton reaches a third, oshb:Isa.48.19.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens where the address returns to the masculine plural after the singular turn that closes at web:Isa.55.5: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier), “Seek Yahweh while he may be found. Call on him while he is near.” (web:Isa.55.6) — the same plural-imperative form-class as the invitation cry's own opening imperatives, now turned to a summons-to-repentance address rather than a continuation of the come-buy-eat invitation of web:Isa.55.1-Isa.55.5. The ways/thoughts contrast follows at כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם דְּרָכָ֑י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.55.8, byte tier), “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways” (web:Isa.55.8), closing with the postpositive divine-speech signature that seals the exhortation's own reasoning. The row runs to the frame boundary at web:Isa.55.13|web:Isa.56.1, where the word's efficacy and the joy-departure close bring the exhortation to its resolution: “It will make a name for Yahweh, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.” (web:Isa.55.13). A setumah paragraph mark (single-witness, tier-3) closes at oshb:Isa.55.5, this row's own front-seam predecessor, and again at oshb:Isa.55.13, this row's own final verse.

The row holds this grammatical turn -- masculine plural giving way to feminine singular at the MT 57:4 | MT 57:6 junction -- as its own live uncertainty rather than a break, since no vocative or frame marker of the tier-1 class accompanies the shift; the row closes at web:Isa.57.13, the verse just before the third-person messenger introduction “He will say” that opens a fresh unit at web:Isa.57.14.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The verse-initial speech-introduction form וְאָמַ֥ר (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.14) launches the command “Build up, build up, prepare the way! Remove the stumbling-block out of the way of my people.” (web:Isa.57.14), opening a fresh unit after the idolatry indictment closes. The divine frame כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א שֹׁכֵ֥ן עַד֙ וְקָד֣וֹשׁ שְׁמ֔וֹ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.15, byte tier) -- “the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy” -- names the speaker before the promise “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.” (web:Isa.57.15) unfolds; the same divine voice continues through the healing promise and the postpositive signature at web:Isa.57.19, where שָׁל֨וֹם שָׁל֜וֹם לָרָח֧וֹק וְלַקָּר֛וֹב אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.57.19, byte tier, a ketiv/qere verse) gives “Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says Yahweh” (web:Isa.57.19). The row holds this healing promise together with its antithetical close, “There is no peace”, says my God, “for the wicked.” (web:Isa.57.21), rather than opening a fresh row at web:Isa.57.20, since the same messenger speech that opened at web:Isa.57.14 governs the contrast as its own resolution.

queue_items.claim: The row's span-cohesion warrant — that first-person-plural verb forms continue through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14 — overreaches its own bytes by two verses.
queue_items.grounds: The last first-person-plural verb in the span is יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם (oshb:Isa.59.12, byte tier). MT 59:13 carries no finite first-person form at all: פָּשֹׁ֤עַ וְכַחֵשׁ֙ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier) and הֹר֧וֹ וְהֹג֛וֹ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier) are infinitives absolute, and its only first-person element is the suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.59.13, byte tier). MT 59:14 carries no first-person form of any kind — וְהֻסַּ֤ג אָחוֹר֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier) opens a third-person summary that runs to the verse's close at וּנְכֹחָ֖ה לֹא תוּכַ֥ל לָבֽוֹא (oshb:Isa.59.14, byte tier). Both seams survive independently (the voice shift at MT 59:9 and the wayyiqtol onset at MT 59:15), so the boundary is not moved by this.

queue_items.claim: The device_notes bracket mis-states where the no-justice phrase stands in MT 59:8: it is mid-verse, not verse-closing.
queue_items.grounds: device_notes calls וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier) 'the no-justice phrase closing the verse just before this row's own front seam'. In MT 59:8 that phrase stands as the fourth and fifth of sixteen tokens, immediately before the athnach at בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָ֑ם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier); the verse actually closes on לֹ֥א יָדַ֖ע שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.59.8, byte tier). The partner claim is correct — אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier) does close MT 59:15 — and both digits re-derive (skeleton tier: 2 verses, Isa 59:8 and 59:15; the justice noun at skeleton tier: 40 verses book-wide, 5 in this chapter).
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: state the MT 59:8 occurrence as mid-verse (before that verse's own caesura) rather than verse-closing, keeping the two digits as swept.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on a voice shift argued from the verb bytes themselves: עַל כֵּ֗ן רָחַ֤ק מִשְׁפָּט֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.9, byte tier) -- “Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness doesn’t overtake us.” (web:Isa.59.9) -- reaches its first true first-person-plural verbs later in the same verse, נְקַוֶּ֤ה and נְהַלֵּֽךְ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.9), “We look for light ... we walk in obscurity.” -- a form-class claim argued from the pointed bytes themselves plus both witnesses' renderings, since no morphology layer is staged for independent verification. The confession continues in first-person-plural verb forms through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14: כָּשַׁ֤לְנוּ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.10), “We stumble at noon as if it were twilight.” (web:Isa.59.10), “We all roar like bears” (web:Isa.59.11), and וַעֲוֺנֹתֵ֖ינוּ יְדַֽעֲנֽוּם (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.12), “our transgressions are multiplied before you ... we know them” (web:Isa.59.12), none of them narrative wayyiqtol forms. The row closes on “Justice is turned away backward, and righteousness stands far away; for truth has fallen in the street, and uprightness can’t enter.” (web:Isa.59.14), the verse just before the wayyiqtol chain that opens the divine-warrior narrative at web:Isa.59.15 -- the row's own closing argument rests on that verb-form shift rather than on the topical content of web:Isa.59.15 alone, since the verse's own first clause is grammatically part of the narrative chain that follows it, not the confession that precedes it.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading attaches the first clause of web:Isa.59.15 ('truth is lacking') to this row as the confession's own summary line, cutting the row at Isa.59.15 rather than Isa.59.14, since its content still catalogues the community's failure of justice.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: communal confession cataloguing societal injustice in first-person-plural voice
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: The oss tag here names the nearest taxonomy class for what is, precisely, a grammatical PERSON/voice shift (third-person description to first-person-plural confession) rather than a change of addressee; no petuchah/setumah break falls at this row's own front seam or within its span in the marks inventory. The no-justice phrase closing the verse just before this row's own front seam, וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט (oshb:Isa.59.8), and the phrase closing the verse just after this row's own rear seam, אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15), share their unprefixed core at skeleton tier (sweep: 2 verses book-wide) and bracket the row's whole span without falling inside it; the broader justice noun that both draw on stands in 40 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, 5 of them in this chapter (Isa.59.8, 59.9, 59.11, 59.14, 59.15). Neither the bracket nor the chapter's density of the term moves either of this row's own seams.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh assertion opens this row, הֵ֛ן לֹֽא קָצְרָ֥ה יַד יְהוָ֖ה מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.1, byte tier) -- “Behold, Yahweh’s hand is not shortened, that it can’t save; nor his ear dull, that it can’t hear.” (web:Isa.59.1); the presentative הֵ֣ן also stands within the preceding unit's own indictment, mid-verse at Isa.58.3 (הֵ֣ן) and verse-initially at Isa.58.4 (oshb:Isa.58.3, oshb:Isa.58.4), matching this verse's הֵ֛ן (oshb:Isa.59.1) at accent-stripped tier only, so the real driver of this row's front seam is the direct address that follows rather than the particle itself: “But your iniquities have separated you and your God” (web:Isa.59.2), continuing in the second person through web:Isa.59.3 before the catalogue of sins shifts into third-person description, “No one sues in righteousness, and no one pleads in truth.” (web:Isa.59.4). No vocative or frame marker interrupts this indictment across the person shift; the row holds web:Isa.59.1-Isa.59.8 as one continuous accusation, closing on “They don’t know the way of peace; and there is no justice in their ways.” (web:Isa.59.8), the verse just before the “therefore” that opens a first-person-plural confession at web:Isa.59.9.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading cuts a fresh row at the second-to-third-person shift of web:Isa.59.4, separating the direct 'your iniquities' accusation of web:Isa.59.1-Isa.59.3 from the impersonal 'they' catalogue of web:Isa.59.4-Isa.59.8, since no explicit frame marker governs either half on its own.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: judgment oracle cataloguing the sins that separate the people from their God

prev_row.device_notes: This row's own front seam, Isa.58.14, carries a setumah break (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only); no other mark falls within this row's own span in the inventory. The row's own closing argument rests on the person shift beginning at Isa.59.9, where the address moves into first-person-plural confession. The row's own closing phrase וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּ֖ט (oshb:Isa.59.8) shares its no-justice core with אֵ֥ין מִשְׁפָּֽט (oshb:Isa.59.15, skeleton tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide), a pairing that sits on this row's own closing verse and its partner past the seam, disclosed here but not argued as a boundary mover. Separately, the salvation root inside this row's own opening splice, מֵֽהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.59.1), returns at וַתּ֤וֹשַֽׁע (oshb:Isa.59.16, byte tier) and in the noun יְשׁוּעָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.59.17, byte tier), an inclusio running past this row's own close that is likewise recorded as texture only.

next_row.boundary_rationale: This row opens where the wayyiqtol narrative chain begins: וַתְּהִ֤י הָֽאֱמֶת֙ נֶעְדֶּ֔רֶת (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.15, byte tier) is itself the chain's first link, continuing directly into וַיַּ֧רְא יְהוָ֛ה וַיֵּ֥רַע בְּעֵינָ֖יו (byte tier) -- “Yahweh saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.” (web:Isa.59.15) -- and on through “He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head.” (web:Isa.59.17), the chain's last wayyiqtol link, וַיַּ֥עַט כַּמְעִ֖יל קִנְאָֽה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.17) -- “and was clad with zeal as a mantle.” (web:Isa.59.17). The chain does not continue into web:Isa.59.18: its verbs כְּעַ֤ל גְּמֻלוֹת֙ כְּעַ֣ל יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.18) are plain imperfects, "he will repay," not wayyiqtol forms, so the repayment of “wrath to his adversaries” (web:Isa.59.18) is a byte-checkable claim argued from the pointed bytes themselves, not a topical extension of the narrative chain. The row keeps the arrival oracle “A Redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who turn from disobedience in Jacob,” says Yahweh. (web:Isa.59.20), closing on its own postpositive signature נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.20), together with the covenant formula that follows rather than closing there, since Isa.59.21 opens its own distinct frame -- וַאֲנִ֗י זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) (oshb:Isa.59.21, byte tier), carrying the doubled speech frame אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה twice in the verse -- “As for me, this is my covenant with them,” says Yahweh. (web:Isa.59.21) -- and reads as the same divine speaker's continuation on a distinguishable frame object rather than an independent fresh oracle. The row closes at web:Isa.59.21; unlike the seams that bound the book's major frames, this junction sits inside a single parent frame and carries no tier-1 signal of its own -- only a tier-3, single-witness parashah mark -- so the rear boundary is held at reduced confidence rather than argued as a frame seam.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading closes a row at the postpositive signature of web:Isa.59.20 and opens a fresh covenant-formula row at web:Isa.59.21, since that verse's fronted first-person pronoun and its own doubled 'says Yahweh' frame could stand as an independent unit.

next_row.device_notes: This row's own closing verse Isa.59.21 carries a setumah break (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only); no other span-relevant mark falls within web:Isa.59.15-Isa.59.21 in the inventory. The wayyiqtol chain launched at Isa.59.15 is a byte-checkable verb-form claim, not a topical one; it is the row's own positive argument for pulling that verse's first clause away from the confession that precedes it. The light-and-rising root standing mid-verse inside this row's own span, וּמִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֖מֶשׁ (oshb:Isa.59.19), runs on past this row's own rear seam through זָרָֽח (oshb:Isa.60.1, byte tier), יִזְרַ֣ח (oshb:Isa.60.2, byte tier), and זַרְחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.60.3, byte tier); the redeemer-and-salvation vocabulary this row's own back half carries also recurs later in the following chapter. queue_items.claim: The rear seam at 61:3 | 61:4 rests on a 'changed subject' that MT 61:4 never states, and the row's own wording concedes the construction runs on across the seam.
queue_items.grounds: The row argues 'Isa.61.4 opens a further waw-plus-perfect clause with a changed subject ... distinct from the mourners just named'. MT 61:4 supplies no nominal subject at all — וּבָנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) and וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) are bare third-person-plural forms whose nearest antecedent is the plural referent named one clause earlier at וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier). The row itself calls 61:4 'a FURTHER waw-plus-perfect clause', i.e. the same construction that closes 61:3, which argues continuity across the seam; and the rejected_alternative's ground, 'Isa.61.4 opens a new finite-verb clause', is non-discriminating because the row has already identified 61:3's own close as a finite waw-plus-perfect clause. A stronger, unused ground stands in the row's own span: the first-person commission voice of 61:1-61:3 has no counterpart from 61:4 onward.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): re-argue the rear seam from the first-person commissioned-speaker frame that ends at 61:3 against the subjectless third-person report opening at MT 61:4, drop the unstated-referent claim, and re-cut rejected_alternative on the replacement warrant — noting that observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and confidence are dependent fields of any driver swap.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A first-person speaker announces a commission, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), matching ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier). A chain of purpose infinitives governed by that same sending — to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty and release, to comfort mourners, to give a garland for ashes — runs to the verse's own caesura at כֵּהָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) and continues, not as a further infinitive but as a waw-plus-perfect finite clause naming the mourners themselves as its subject, וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier): “that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.” (web:Isa.61.3), matching מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier). Isa.61.4 opens a further waw-plus-perfect clause with a changed subject, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) — the third-person-plural community now rebuilding, distinct from the mourners just named and called a planting at the unit's own close — marking this unit's close.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the first-person mission statement as continuing through Isa.61.4's building report was rejected because the infinitive-purpose chain governed by Yahweh's sending closes at Isa.61.3's own glorification clause, and Isa.61.4 opens a new finite-verb clause with a third-person-plural subject. Labeling the unit servant_song was considered and set aside because this unit's own bytes lack the eved-root vocabulary that anchors the book's servant census, leaving the anointed speaker's identity an open question the unit does not resolve.
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) at oshb:Isa.60.22 closes the preceding unit immediately before this one opens; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.61.3, inside this unit's own span. The catchword closing this unit is tier-mixed, not uniformly byte-true: the 'to be glorified' verb is byte-identical between the two units, לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) and לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), but the paired planting noun is not — oshb:Isa.60.21 stages the ketiv/qere pair מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere) against this unit's own מַטַּ֥ע (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), the two meeting only at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide on that consonantal string). This tier-mixed catchword is disclosed here rather than treated as evidence against the boundary already argued from the subject shift at Isa.61.4. Labeling this unit servant_song was weighed and set aside: this unit's own bytes (Isa.61.1-Isa.61.3) lack the eved-root servant vocabulary that anchors the book's own servant census, so the identity of the anointed first-person speaker stays an open question this unit does not resolve.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A second-person-feminine-singular imperative pair opens the unit, “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh's glory has risen on you!” (web:Isa.60.1), matching ק֥וּמִי א֖וֹרִי (oshb:Isa.60.1, byte tier). The same addressee is sustained through further imperative and declarative movements — nations and kings drawn to her light, sons and daughters carried home, foreign wealth and foreign service given to her, her gates kept open — without an explicit change of addressee or scene across the chapter. A recognition-formula clause partway through, “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.” (web:Isa.60.16), matching וְיָדַ֗עַתְּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.60.16, byte tier), is not repeated at the unit's own close: “I, Yahweh, will do this quickly in its time.” (web:Isa.60.22), matching אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּעִתָּ֥הּ אֲחִישֶֽׁנָּה (oshb:Isa.60.22, byte tier), which carries no knowing-verb at all, so the two clauses share only the two-token self-declaration אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ / אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה — a pairing that differs at byte tier and meets from accent-stripped tier down, where it stands in 22 verses book-wide. Even at that lighter tier, the repeated self-declaration frames an internal turn rather than marking a second addressee. Isa.61.1 opens a new first-person speaker frame, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), sharing no addressee with this chapter's second-person Zion address, and closes this unit. This row's span is the entirety of chapter 60 (22 verses in the book's own inventory), so under the campaign's whole-chapter rule its confidence is held at the medium_low ceiling rather than assigned a lower band, and that ceiling reflects the span's shape, not any new defect found in it.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the chapter at the self-declaration echo between Isa.60.16 and Isa.60.22 was rejected because neither occurrence brings an explicit change of addressee or scene inside the same second-person-feminine-singular address; the echo itself differs at byte tier and meets from accent-stripped tier down, where it stands in 22 verses book-wide, since Isa.60.22 carries the bare two-token self-declaration with no knowing-verb, unlike Isa.60.16's full recognition formula.

prev_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) marks the parashah layer at oshb:Isa.59.21, immediately before this unit opens, and again at oshb:Isa.60.22, at its own close — tier-3 corroboration for both edges; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.60.9, completing the span-relevant symmetry sweep for MT 60.1-60.22 across the parashah, paseq, and ketiv/qere layers. Isa.60.21 stages both the ketiv and qere forms of the planting noun side by side, נֵ֧צֶר מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֖י לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) — the unpointed ketiv מטעו carries a third-person-masculine-singular suffix ('his planting'), the pointed qere מַטָּעַ֛י a first-person-singular suffix ('my planting'); the two forms differ by suffix person, not number, and this is a single-witness note read either way. The same planting-root vocabulary paired with the 'to be glorified' verb recurs in the following unit's own close (web:Isa.61.3), a catchword this unit's own boundary does not erase. The qadosh-Israel title, a signature title spanning both halves of the book (25 verses swept per attested spelling: 24 at the standard plene spelling, plus the separately-attested defective spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.49.7, byte tier)), recurs at web:Isa.60.9 and web:Isa.60.14 inside this span as in-unit texture, not a boundary driver.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A finite third-person-plural clause, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), matching וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), opens a report of the community's restoration that continues through an explicit address shift, “But you will be called Yahweh's priests.” (web:Isa.61.6), matching וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier), and a first-person divine declaration, “For I, Yahweh, love justice.” (web:Isa.61.8), matching כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֹהֵ֣ב מִשְׁפָּ֔ט (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier), none of these bringing a vocative or scene marker distinct from the same covenant promise. The unit closes on the blessed-offspring report, “that they are the offspring which Yahweh has blessed.” (web:Isa.61.9), before Isa.61.10 opens with a fresh first-person voice, “I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh!” (web:Isa.61.10), sharing no stated referent with the third-person offspring just named.
